extracted.intended_audience: public water system owners/operators, state drinking water regulators, and laboratories performing drinking water analyses
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements (40 CFR part 141) for monitoring, sampling, analytical methods, reporting, and related compliance procedures for public water systems (coliforms, turbidity, arsenic, nitrates, PFAS, etc.). Useful for systems, state agencies, and labs implementing or reviewing compliance programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: PFAS subpart Z effective and compliance dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations pertaining to the per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) chemicals set forth in subpart Z of this part are effective June 25, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 141.900 for the compliance dates for provisions under subpart Z. Compliance with reporting requirements under subpart Z, in accordance with subparts O (consumer confidence rule) and Q (public notification rule) are required on April 26, 2027, except for notification requirements in § 141.203 related to violations of the MCLs. The compliance date for the PFAS MCLs in § 141.61 (as specified in § 141.60) and for § 141.203 notifications of violations of the PFAS MCLs is April 26, 2029.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arsenic MCL applicability and analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The maximum contaminant level for arsenic applies only to community water systems; analyses and determination of compliance with the 0.05 mg/L MCL for arsenic use the requirements of § 141.23.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The arsenic MCL is 0.05 milligrams per liter for community water systems until January 23, 2006.

rubrics_metrics.name: State discretion for higher nitrate level in non-community systems
rubrics_metrics.description: At the discretion of the State, nitrate levels not to exceed 20 mg/L may be allowed in a non-community water system if the supplier demonstrates to the satisfaction of the State certain conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions: (1) such water will not be available to children under 6 months of age; (2) the non-community system is meeting public notification requirements under § 141.209 including continuous posting that nitrate levels exceed 10 mg/L and the potential health effects; (3) local and State public health authorities will be notified annually of nitrate levels that exceed 10 mg/L; and (4) no adverse health effects shall result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turbidity maximum contaminant levels and exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum contaminant levels for turbidity measured at representative entry point(s) to distribution system: (a) One turbidity unit (TU) as determined by monthly average pursuant to § 141.22, except up to five TU may be allowed if supplier demonstrates to State that higher turbidity does not interfere with disinfection, prevent maintenance of effective disinfectant throughout distribution, or interfere with microbiological determinations; (b) Five TU based on an average for two consecutive days pursuant to § 141.22.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to community and non-community water systems using surface water sources in whole or in part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written sample siting plan for total coliform sampling
rubrics_metrics.description: Public water systems must collect total coliform samples at sites which are representative of water throughout the distribution system according to a written sample siting plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These sample siting plans are subject to State review and revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total coliform monitoring frequency for community water systems
rubrics_metrics.description: The monitoring frequency for total coliforms for community water systems is based on population served (detailed minimum number of samples per month table by population).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a community system serving 25–1,000 persons has no history of total coliform contamination in its current configuration and a sanitary survey in past five years shows protected groundwater source and no sanitary defects, the State may reduce monitoring frequency but not less than one sample per quarter; State must approve reduced frequency in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total coliform monitoring frequency for non-community water systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitoring frequency rules for non-community water systems depend on source type and population: (i) groundwater-only systems serving ≤1,000 must monitor each calendar quarter water is provided (State may reduce in writing but not to less than once/year beginning June 29, 1994); (ii) groundwater-only systems serving >1,000 in any month must monitor at same frequency as like-sized community systems (State may reduce for months serving ≤1,000 but not less than once/year); (iii) non-community systems using surface water must monitor at same frequency as like-sized community systems; (iv) groundwater under direct influence of surface water must monitor at same frequency as like-sized community systems and begin within six months of State determination that GW is under direct influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to definitions in § 141.2; State reductions must be in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample timing and special turbidity-triggered sampling
rubrics_metrics.description: Public water system must collect samples at regular time intervals throughout the month; systems using only groundwater (except GWUDI) and serving ≤4,900 may collect all required samples on a single day if taken from different sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems that use surface water or GWUDI and do not practice filtration per Subpart H must collect at least one sample near the first service connection each day the turbidity level of the source water exceeds 1 NTU; this coliform sample must be analyzed within 24 hours of the first exceedance unless State determines analysis within 30 hours is necessary due to logistics. These sample results count toward MCL compliance in § 141.63.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special purpose samples excluded from compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Special purpose samples (e.g., taken to determine whether disinfection is sufficient following pipe placement, replacement, or repair) shall not be used to determine compliance with the MCL for total coliforms in § 141.63.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeat samples taken pursuant to paragraph (b) are not considered special purpose samples and must be used to determine compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeat monitoring requirements after a total coliform-positive routine sample
rubrics_metrics.description: If a routine sample is total coliform-positive, the public water system must collect a set of repeat samples within 24 hours of being notified. Systems collecting >1 routine sample/month must collect at least 3 repeat samples for each positive; systems collecting ≤1 routine sample/month must collect at least 4 repeat samples for each positive. State may extend 24-hour limit case-by-case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At least one repeat sample must be from the original sampling tap, at least one within five service connections upstream, and at least one within five service connections downstream (State may waive upstream/downstream for end-of-system taps). All repeat samples must be collected same day except State may allow single-service-connection systems to collect over four days or collect larger volume repeat samples totaling at least 400 ml (300 ml for systems collecting >1 routine sample/month). If any repeat in the set is positive, an additional set must be collected within 24 hours (or extended time) and repeat until either a complete set is negative or system determines MCL exceeded and notifies State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional routine sampling requirement and waiver process for small-sample systems
rubrics_metrics.description: If a system collecting fewer than five routine samples/month has one or more total coliform-positive samples and the State does not invalidate the sample(s), it must collect at least five routine samples during the next month the system provides water to the public, unless the State waives this requirement under specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State may waive the five-sample requirement if (i) State or approved agent performs a site visit before end of next month (detailed enough to determine need for monitoring/corrective actions) — the system's employee cannot perform the site visit even if an agent; or (ii) State determines cause of positive sample and documents in writing that system corrected or will correct problem before end of next month, documented and approved by supervisor, and made available to EPA and public. State cannot waive solely because repeats are negative. Under this paragraph, system must still take at least one routine sample before end of next month for compliance determination unless State documented prior correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting of subsequent samples as repeat samples
rubrics_metrics.description: If after collecting a routine sample and before learning its results the system collects another routine sample(s) from within five adjacent service connections of the initial sample, and the initial is later found total coliform-positive, the system may count the subsequent sample(s) as repeat samples instead of routine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of routine and repeat samples in compliance determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Results of all routine and repeat samples not invalidated by the State must be included in determining compliance with the MCL for total coliforms in § 141.63.

rubrics_metrics.name: State invalidation criteria for total coliform-positive samples
rubrics_metrics.description: The State may invalidate a total coliform-positive sample only if conditions of (i), (ii), or (iii) are met: (i) laboratory establishes improper sample analysis caused the result; (ii) State determines on basis of repeat results that positive resulted from domestic or other non-distribution plumbing problem (with specified repeat-sample pattern restrictions); (iii) State has substantial grounds to believe the result is due to circumstance not reflecting distribution water quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To invalidate under (iii), system must still collect all required repeat samples; decision and rationale must be documented in writing, approved and signed by supervisor of State official who recommended it, made available to EPA and the public, and must state specific cause and corrective actions. State may not invalidate solely because all repeats are negative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory invalidation criteria for total coliform samples due to analytical interference
rubrics_metrics.description: A laboratory must invalidate a total coliform sample (unless total coliforms are detected) if the sample produces a turbid culture without gas production using a gas-formation method, produces a turbid culture without acid reaction in P-A test, or exhibits confluent growth or colonies too numerous to count with membrane filter methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If laboratory invalidates a sample for such interference, the system must collect another sample from the same location within 24 hours of being notified and have it analyzed; continue to re-sample within 24 hours until a valid result is obtained. State may waive 24-hour limit case-by-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanitary survey requirements and frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Public water systems that do not collect five or more routine samples/month must undergo an initial sanitary survey by June 29, 1994 for community systems and June 29, 1999 for non-community systems. Thereafter, systems must undergo another sanitary survey every five years, except certain non-community protected groundwater systems must undergo subsequent surveys at least every ten years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State must review sanitary survey results to determine adequacy of monitoring frequency and needed measures. Sanitary surveys must be performed by the State or an agent approved by the State; system is responsible for ensuring survey occurs. Surveys conducted by the State under § 142.16(o)(2) may be used to meet these requirements. In States with EPA-approved wellhead protection programs, existing contamination-source information collected for that program may be considered instead of collecting new information if collected since last sanitary survey.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fecal coliform / Escherichia coli follow-up testing and notification
rubrics_metrics.description: If any routine or repeat sample is total coliform-positive, the system must analyze that culture medium to determine if fecal coliforms are present, except the system may test for E. coli in lieu of fecal coliforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fecal coliforms or E. coli are present, the system must notify the State by the end of the day when notified of the result, unless notified after the State office is closed, in which case notify before the end of next business day. State may, case-by-case, allow a system to forgo fecal coliform or E. coli testing if the system assumes the sample is fecal/E. coli-positive; system must notify State as specified and provisions of § 141.63(b) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical methodology general requirements for total coliforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard sample volume for total coliform analysis is 100 ml. Public water systems need only determine presence or absence of total coliforms; density determination is not required. Systems must conduct analyses in accordance with one of the analytical methods listed in the regulation or alternative methods in appendix A to subpart C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation lists approved methods (e.g., Total Coliform Fermentation Technique, Membrane Filter Technique, Presence-Absence Test, ONPG-MUG, Colisure, E*Colite, m-ColiBlue24, Readycult, Chromocult, Colitag) and references to Standard Methods editions and incorporation by reference details. Time from sample collection to initiation of analysis may not exceed 30 hours; systems are encouraged (not required) to hold samples below 10°C during transit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory evaluation of false-positive and false-negative rates
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA strongly recommends laboratories evaluate false-positive and false-negative rates for method(s) they use for monitoring total coliforms and encourages establishing these rates within their own laboratory and sample matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency suggests labs perform studies on a minimum of 5% of all total coliform-positive samples (except methods where verification/confirmation is already required). Methods for establishing rates may be based on lactose fermentation, rapid β-galactosidase and cytochrome oxidase tests, multi-test identification systems, or equivalent confirmation tests. False-positive/negative information may be available in published studies or from manufacturers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fecal coliform analysis procedure from total coliform-positive cultures
rubrics_metrics.description: When MTF or P-A Coliform Test used, shake lactose-positive presumptive tube or P-A vigorously and transfer growth into brilliant green lactose bile broth and EC medium to determine presence of total and fecal coliforms. For membrane filter methods, transfer total coliform-positive culture by specific methods to EC medium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incubate inoculated tubes in waterbath at 44.5 ±0.2 °C for 24 ±2 hours. Gas production of any amount in inner fermentation tube of EC medium indicates a positive fecal coliform test. Preparation of EC medium described in Standard Methods (Method 9221E); only presence/absence required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved analytical methods and method-specific requirements for E. coli
rubrics_metrics.description: Public water systems must conduct E. coli analyses according to specified methods or alternatives in appendix A: (i) EC medium + 50 µg/mL MUG with incubation at 44.5 ±0.2 °C for 24 ±2 hours (observe fluorescence under 366 nm UV if using older edition); (ii) nutrient agar + 100 µg/mL MUG as described; (iii) MMO-MUG Test (Autoanalysis Colilert is MMO-MUG); (iv) Colisure Test; (v–x) membrane filter with MI agar, E*Colite, m-ColiBlue24, Readycult, Chromocult, Colitag.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific procedural notes include incubation times, fluorescence observation, option to incubate an additional 4 hours if fluorescence questionable (but not exceed 28 hours total), use of hepes buffer as the only approved MMO-MUG formulation for E. coli detection, and option to transfer culture to EC Medium + MUG for further analysis. References and sources for method descriptions and incorporation by reference are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response and reporting requirements for total coliform MCL and monitoring violations
rubrics_metrics.description: A public water system that has exceeded the MCL for total coliforms in § 141.63 must report the violation to the State no later than the end of the next business day after it learns of the violation, and notify the public in accordance with subpart Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A public water system that failed to comply with a coliform monitoring requirement, including sanitary survey requirement, must report the monitoring violation to the State within ten days after the system discovers the violation, and notify the public in accordance with subpart Q.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability transition to subpart Y
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of paragraphs (a) and (d) of § 141.21 are applicable until March 31, 2016. The provisions of paragraphs (b), (c), (e), (f), and (g) of § 141.21 are applicable until all required repeat monitoring and fecal coliform or E. coli testing initiated by total coliform-positive samples taken before April 1, 2016 are completed, as well as associated analytical method, reporting, recordkeeping, public notification, and consumer confidence report requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beginning April 1, 2016, the provisions of subpart Y are applicable, with systems required to begin regular monitoring at the same frequency as the system-specific frequency required on March 31, 2016.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turbidity sampling frequency and applicability for filtered/unfiltered systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements in § 141.22 apply to unfiltered systems until December 30, 1991 unless State determined prior to that date that filtration is required; apply to filtered systems until June 29, 1993; apply to unfiltered systems the State has determined must install filtration until June 29, 1993 or until filtration is installed, whichever is later. Samples shall be taken by suppliers for both community and non-community water systems at a representative entry point(s) at least once per day to make turbidity measurements to determine compliance with § 141.13.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the State determines that a reduced sampling frequency in a non-community will not pose a risk to public health, it can reduce the required sampling frequency.
